newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower in listless trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower in thin trade on Tuesday as uncertainties about Japan's financial sector and interest rates, combined with a dearth of buying incentives, depressed activity.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract lost 235 points to end at 19,925 on low volume of 12,190 lots.
"The market stayed rather weak since the start today. Fears of a rate hike are putting pressure on the equity market, but I believe it will pick up," a dealer at a European house said.
He added, however, that traders were likely to sell into any rallies towards the 20,150 area.
But a trader with a U.S. institution said the June Nikkei had been well supported around the low of 19,850 in recent sessions and he expected it to head higher.
"I'm still a bull. My minimum objective is 20,285 and if we break that, it could go all the way to 20,650," he added.

On Taiwan futures, the May contract ended lower at 347.9 on volume of 758 lots as players rolled over their positions ahead of the contract's expiry on Friday. April was also down to 345.9 on 697 lots.
